rubric_additions.rubric-11:
Rule: If we add or change Go code that builds the Resource by combining supplied attributes with detected ones, check the detector order and which value wins.
Example: The operator supplies host.name=payments-host and the selected host detector finds machine-host. Run the actual setup and check that the promised payments-host value survives.
Evidence: Scope and required checks: When this change adds or modifies application-owned Go Resource initialization that combines supplied attributes with native/default detectors, inspect the actual detector order and merge precedence. If the selected initialization sources can overwrite an operator-owned attribute we promise to preserve, test a representative collision through that same initialization and proof boundary. Checking only service.name would not prove that host.name survives a later detector. Other representative colliding keys and values are valid; do not add a host detector just to reproduce this example. Audit plans the check; implementation and verification prove the selected owned path. Do not add custom parsers or certify unchanged, unselected detectors.
Insufficient evidence: A service.name-only helper used to claim another attribute survives a later detector.
rubric_additions.rubric-12:
Rule: If the Go code in scope reads a standard OTel true/false setting, test that it follows OTel's rules.
Example: For the selected standard Boolean reader, TrUe means true; 1, t and a space-padded true do not.
Evidence: Sources: OpenTelemetry Boolean environment rules (https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/otel/configuration/sdk-environment-variables/#boolean) and Go strconv.ParseBool (https://pkg.go.dev/strconv#ParseBool). Scope and required checks: For a selected or newly application-owned Go reader of a standard environment Boolean, test the actual reader and resulting branch with raw true/TrUe, nontrue 1/t/T, and space-padded true. Only the raw literal true, ignoring letter case, is true: TrUe qualifies, but ' true ' does not. Trimming a selector or using strconv.ParseBool without qualification is not equivalent. Keep invalid-nonempty warning behavior at SHOULD strength. Preserve unchanged SDK and file-loader ownership; do not require tests for unused SDK parser combinations.
Insufficient evidence: Trimming the input or relying on strconv.ParseBool as if it had the required raw-literal behavior.
rubric_additions.rubric-22:
Rule: Before replacing Go's process-wide slog default, inspect where the captured handler really writes.
Example: A captured built-in slog handler can route through the standard logger that SetDefault subsequently redirects, creating a cycle when that handler is nested in the new default.
Evidence: The built-in default can route dynamically through the standard logger, which SetDefault rewires; putting that captured handler inside the new default can therefore recurse or deadlock. An application-owned logger may retain the handler without changing the process default. A writer adapter alone does not prove preservation of native formatting or level markers. Assert the original enablement, format, sinks, owner and record count. Keep this native-logging cycle separate from SDK diagnostic feedback. Reuse an existing safe route rather than forcing a handler replacement.
Insufficient evidence: A writer adapter without checking the actual output route, native format, enablement and record counts.
rubric_additions.rubric-25:
Rule: The untouched Go fixture logs with slog.Warn inside a goroutine without request context. Plan, repair or check that log's join to the real request, according to your role.
Example: The fixture calls slog.Warn inside a goroutine without caller context. A selected repair must join that goroutine log to its real request SDK context.
Evidence: Audit must plan request-context transfer and acceptance checks for a context-aware log call. Instrumentation repairs this boundary if it is still missing. Verification checks the current real request-to-async SDK-context join without editing code. Do not report a path that is already repaired as a remaining context-transfer gap.
Insufficient evidence: Calling a context helper separately without testing the actual request-to-goroutine log path.
